203: int bk7258_psram_shutdown(void)
204: {
205:   unsigned int i;
206: 
207:   nxmutex_lock(&g_psram_lock);
208:   if (g_state != BK7258_PSRAM_ONLINE)
209:     {
210:       nxmutex_unlock(&g_psram_lock);
211:       return -ENODEV;
212:     }
213: 
214:   g_state = BK7258_PSRAM_FREEZING;
215:   if (g_heap_allocations != 0)
216:     {
217:       g_state = BK7258_PSRAM_ONLINE;
218:       nxmutex_unlock(&g_psram_lock);
219:       return -EBUSY;
220:     }
221: 
222:   for (i = 0; i < BK7258_PSRAM_POOL_COUNT; i++)
223:     {
224:       if (g_pool_allocations[i] != 0)
225:         {
226:           g_state = BK7258_PSRAM_ONLINE;
227:           nxmutex_unlock(&g_psram_lock);
228:           return -EBUSY;
229:         }
230:     }
231: 
232:   mm_uninitialize(g_psram_heap);
233:   g_psram_heap = NULL;
234:   for (i = 0; i < BK7258_PSRAM_POOL_COUNT; i++)
235:     {
236:       mm_uninitialize(g_pool_heap[i]);
237:       g_pool_heap[i] = NULL;
238:     }
239: 
240:   g_state = BK7258_PSRAM_OFFLINE;
241:   nxmutex_unlock(&g_psram_lock);
242:   return OK;
243: }

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

4: 
5: #include <nuttx/config.h>
6: 
7: #include <stdbool.h>
8: #include <stdint.h>
9: 
10: #include <nuttx/irq.h>
11: #include <nuttx/spinlock.h>
12: 
13: #include "arm_internal.h"
14: #include "hardware/bk7258_gpio.h"
15: 
16: void bk7258_gpio_input_pullup(unsigned int pin)
17: {
18:   irqstate_t flags;
19: 
20:   flags = enter_critical_section();
21:   modifyreg32(BK7258_GPIO_CFG(pin),
22:               BK7258_GPIO_OUTPUT | BK7258_GPIO_SECOND_FUNCTION,
23:               BK7258_GPIO_INPUT_ENABLE | BK7258_GPIO_OUTPUT_DISABLE |
24:               BK7258_GPIO_PULL_UP | BK7258_GPIO_PULL_ENABLE);
25:   leave_critical_section(flags);
26: }
27: 
28: void bk7258_gpio_output(unsigned int pin, bool value)
29: {
30:   irqstate_t flags;
31:   uint32_t setbits = value ? BK7258_GPIO_OUTPUT : 0;
32: 
33:   flags = enter_critical_section();
34:   modifyreg32(BK7258_GPIO_CFG(pin),
35:               BK7258_GPIO_INPUT_ENABLE | BK7258_GPIO_OUTPUT |
36:               BK7258_GPIO_OUTPUT_DISABLE | BK7258_GPIO_PULL_ENABLE |
37:               BK7258_GPIO_SECOND_FUNCTION,
38:               setbits);
39:   leave_critical_section(flags);
40: }
41: 
42: void bk7258_gpio_write(unsigned int pin, bool value)
43: {
44:   if (value)
45:     {
46:       modifyreg32(BK7258_GPIO_CFG(pin), 0, BK7258_GPIO_OUTPUT);
47:     }
48:   else
49:     {
50:       modifyreg32(BK7258_GPIO_CFG(pin), BK7258_GPIO_OUTPUT, 0);
51:     }
52: }
53: 
54: bool bk7258_gpio_read(unsigned int pin)
55: {
56:   return (getreg32(BK7258_GPIO_CFG(pin)) & BK7258_GPIO_INPUT) != 0;
57: }
58: 
59: void bk7258_gpio_set_function(unsigned int pin, unsigned int function)
60: {
61:   irqstate_t flags;
62:   uintptr_t regaddr = BK7258_GPIO_SYS_CFG(pin);
63:   uint32_t shift = BK7258_GPIO_SYS_SHIFT(pin);
64: 
65:   flags = enter_critical_section();
66:   modifyreg32(regaddr, BK7258_GPIO_SYS_MASK(pin), (function & 0xfu) << shift);
67:   modifyreg32(BK7258_GPIO_CFG(pin),
68:               BK7258_GPIO_INPUT_ENABLE | BK7258_GPIO_OUTPUT |
69:               BK7258_GPIO_PULL_ENABLE,
70:               BK7258_GPIO_OUTPUT_DISABLE | BK7258_GPIO_SECOND_FUNCTION);
71:   leave_critical_section(flags);

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * BK7258 Armino-compatible HW_CTRL power-up and heartbeat service.
3:  ****************************************************************************/
4: 
5: #include <nuttx/config.h>
6: 
7: #include <errno.h>
8: #include <stdbool.h>
9: #include <stdint.h>
10: #include <stdio.h>
11: #include <string.h>
12: #include <syslog.h>
13: 
14: #include <nuttx/clock.h>
15: #include <nuttx/kthread.h>
16: #include <nuttx/mutex.h>
17: #include <nuttx/signal.h>
18: 
19: #include "hardware/bk7258_mbox.h"
20: #define IPC_CPU1_POWER_UP_INDICATION   1u
21: #define IPC_CPU1_HEART_BEAT_INDICATION 2u
22: #define IPC_ACK_STATE_COMPLETE         2u
23: #define IPC_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS        600u
24: #define IPC_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL         MSEC2TICK(2000)
25: #define IPC_HEARTBEAT_RETRY            MSEC2TICK(100)
26: #define IPC_HEARTBEAT_POLL_US           10000u
27: #define IPC_HEARTBEAT_PRIORITY          110
28: 
29: static mutex_t g_ipc_lock = NXMUTEX_INITIALIZER;
30: static volatile int g_ipc_ack_result;
31: static volatile int g_ipc_start_result;
32: static volatile int g_heartbeat_result;
33: static volatile bool g_heartbeat_enabled;
34: static volatile bool g_heartbeat_pending;
35: static volatile uint32_t g_heartbeat_completions;
36: static clock_t g_next_heartbeat;
37: static uint32_t g_heartbeat_failures;
38: static uint32_t g_heartbeat_submissions;
39: static uint32_t g_heartbeat_reported;
40: static bool g_ipc_started;
41: 
42: static int ipc_ack_result(const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *ack,
43:                           int result)
44: {
45:   if (result == OK &&
46:       (ack == NULL || ack->reserved != IPC_ACK_STATE_COMPLETE))
47:     {
48:       result = -EREMOTEIO;
49:     }
50: 
51:   return result;
52: }
53: 
54: static void ipc_tx_complete(const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *ack,
55:                             int result, void *arg)
56: {
57:   g_ipc_ack_result = ipc_ack_result(ack, result);
58:   if ((uintptr_t)arg == IPC_CPU1_POWER_UP_INDICATION &&
59:       g_ipc_ack_result == OK)
60:     {
61:       g_heartbeat_result = OK;
62:       g_next_heartbeat = clock_systime_ticks() + IPC_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL;
63:       g_heartbeat_enabled = true;
64:     }
65: }
66: 
67: static void ipc_heartbeat_complete(
68:   const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *ack, int result, void *arg)
69: {
70:   (void)arg;
71:   g_heartbeat_result = ipc_ack_result(ack, result);
72:   g_heartbeat_completions++;
73:   g_heartbeat_pending = false;
74: }
75: 
76: static int ipc_send(uint8_t command, uint32_t parameter)
77: {
78:   struct bk7258_mb_wire_message message;
79:   volatile uint32_t *payload =
80:     (volatile uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)BK7258_IPC_TX_ADDRESS;
81:   int ret;
82: 
83:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&g_ipc_lock);
84:   if (ret < 0)
85:     {
86:       return ret;
87:     }
88: 
89:   *payload = parameter;
90:   __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
91: 
92:   memset(&message, 0, sizeof(message));
93:   message.header = command;
94:   message.payload_address = BK7258_IPC_TX_ADDRESS;
95:   message.payload_length =
96:     command == IPC_CPU1_HEART_BEAT_INDICATION ? sizeof(*payload) : 0;
97:   g_ipc_ack_result = -EINPROGRESS;
98: 
99:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_send_wire(BK7258_MB_CHAN_HW_CTRL_TX, &message,
100:                                   ipc_tx_complete,
101:                                   (void *)(uintptr_t)command);
102:   if (ret == OK)
103:     {
104:       ret = bk7258_mailbox_wait_hw_control(IPC_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS);
105:       if (ret == OK)
106:         {
107:           ret = g_ipc_ack_result;
108:         }
109:     }
110: 
111:   nxmutex_unlock(&g_ipc_lock);
112:   return ret > 0 ? -EIO : ret;
113: }
114: 
115: static int ipc_heartbeat_worker(int argc, char **argv)
116: {
117:   (void)argc;
118:   (void)argv;
119: 
120:   for (;;)
121:     {
122:       nxsig_usleep(IPC_HEARTBEAT_POLL_US);
123:       bk7258_ipc_heartbeat_poll();
124:     }
125: 
126:   return OK;
127: }
128: 
129: void bk7258_ipc_heartbeat_poll(void)
130: {
131:   struct bk7258_mb_wire_message message;
132:   volatile uint32_t *payload =
133:     (volatile uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)BK7258_IPC_TX_ADDRESS;
134:   clock_t now;
135:   int ret;
136: 
137:   if (!g_heartbeat_enabled || g_heartbeat_pending)
138:     {
139:       return;
140:     }
141: 
142:   if (g_heartbeat_completions != g_heartbeat_reported)
143:     {
144:       g_heartbeat_reported = g_heartbeat_completions;
145:       if (g_heartbeat_reported <= 3u)
146:         {
147:           printf("IPC: heartbeat ACK result=%d count=%lu\n",
148:                  g_heartbeat_result,
149:                  (unsigned long)g_heartbeat_reported);
150:         }
151:     }
152: 
153:   if (g_heartbeat_result < 0)
154:     {
155:       g_heartbeat_failures++;
156:       if ((g_heartbeat_failures & (g_heartbeat_failures - 1u)) == 0)
157:         {
158:           syslog(LOG_ERR, "IPC heartbeat failed: %d count=%lu\n",
159:                  g_heartbeat_result,
160:                  (unsigned long)g_heartbeat_failures);
161:         }
162: 
163:       g_heartbeat_result = OK;
164:     }
165: 
166:   now = clock_systime_ticks();
167:   if ((sclock_t)(now - g_next_heartbeat) < 0)
168:     {
169:       return;
170:     }
171: 
172:   *payload = 0;
173:   __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
174:   memset(&message, 0, sizeof(message));
175:   message.header = IPC_CPU1_HEART_BEAT_INDICATION;
176:   message.payload_address = BK7258_IPC_TX_ADDRESS;
177:   message.payload_length = sizeof(*payload);
178:   g_heartbeat_result = -EINPROGRESS;
179:   g_heartbeat_pending = true;
180:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_send_wire(BK7258_MB_CHAN_HW_CTRL_TX, &message,
181:                                  ipc_heartbeat_complete, NULL);
182:   if (ret == OK)
183:     {
184:       g_heartbeat_submissions++;
185:       g_next_heartbeat = now + IPC_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL;
186:       if (g_heartbeat_submissions <= 3u)
187:         {

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_qspi.c
3:  *
4:  * BK7258 QSPI1 command-channel driver (no DMA, cmd_c/cmd_d indirect command
5:  * path only).  Register layout source: bk_avdk_smp release/v3.1.1
6:  * ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/qspi_struct.h and hal/qspi_ll.h.  QSPI0
7:  * and QSPI1 are two identical controller instances differing only in base
8:  * address and which fixed GPIO group is wired to their CLK/CSN/IO0-3
9:  * signal lines.
10:  *
11:  * Corrected from QSPI0 to QSPI1 (2026-07-31): this driver originally
12:  * targeted QSPI0 (base 0x46040000, GPIO22/23/24/25) because that is the
13:  * pin group used by bk_avdk_smp's generic
14:  * projects/spi_lcd_example/qspi_lcd_example reference configs. Those
15:  * reference projects' own hardware wires their LCD to that pin group, but
16:  * this board's actual schematic
17:  * (AIDK_AI玩具开发板_原理图.pdf sheet 2/6 main chip pin table + sheet 5/6
18:  * CN5 single-screen connector) shows the panel's LCD_QSPI_CLK/CS/D0/D1 net
19:  * labels are wired to chip pins 35/34/33/32 = P2/P3/P4/P5 =
20:  * GPIO2/GPIO3/GPIO4/GPIO5, which per the chip's pinmux table
21:  * (bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/gpio_map.h GPIO_DEV_MAP)
22:  * carry QSPI1_CLK/QSPI1_CSN/QSPI1_IO0/QSPI1_IO1 (function-select index 6),
23:  * not QSPI0.  Symptom that led to this fix: with the QSPI0 assumption,
24:  * bk7258_qspi0_send_cmd() always timed out on the very first init command
25:  * (0xFE) -- GPIO22-25 were pinmuxed to QSPI0, but the panel is not
26:  * physically wired to those pins, so cmd_start_done never asserts and the
27:  * 10000-iteration wait always exhausts.  See
28:  * hardware/bk7258_memorymap.h's BK7258_QSPI1_BASE comment for the full
29:  * schematic evidence chain (chip pin numbers, net names, gpio_map.h
30:  * excerpt).
31:  *
32:  * Note the schematic's literal net names ("LCD_QSPI_D0" etc.) do NOT
33:  * match the SoC's real hardware role for these pins (CLK/CSN, not data
34:  * lines) -- PCB net labels are the board designer's arbitrary
35:  * connector-pin numbering convention, not a statement about which SoC
36:  * peripheral function is actually multiplexed onto that pad.  The real
37:  * role is only knowable from gpio_map.h's per-pin function array, which is
38:  * what this driver's pin/function assignments below are built from.
39:  *
40:  * Register offsets (byte offset from BK7258_QSPI1_BASE, word index in
41:  * qspi_hw_t from qspi_struct.h in parentheses) -- identical layout to
42:  * QSPI0, only the base address differs:
43:  *   glb_ctrl    0x08 (REG_0x02) - bit[0] soft_reset, bit[1] bps_clkgate
44:  *   cmd_c_l     0x40 (REG_0x10)
45:  *   cmd_c_h     0x44 (REG_0x11)
46:  *   cmd_c_cfg1  0x48 (REG_0x12)
47:  *   cmd_c_cfg2  0x4c (REG_0x13) - bit[0] cmd_start
48:  *   cmd_d_l     0x50 (REG_0x14)
49:  *   cmd_d_h     0x54 (REG_0x15)
50:  *   cmd_d_cfg1  0x58 (REG_0x16)
51:  *   cmd_d_cfg2  0x5c (REG_0x17) - bit[0] cmd_start
52:  *   status      0x70 (REG_0x1c) - bit[2] cmd_start_done
53:  *   status_clr  0x6c (REG_0x1b) - bit[2] clr_cmd_start_done
54:  *
55:  * The "command done" flag is carried by the status register's
56:  * cmd_start_done bit, not by core_status (REG_0x03, byte offset 0x0c),
57:  * which is an unused, un-bitfielded raw word in the vendor headers and is
58:  * never read by qspi_ll_is_cmd_start_done()/qspi_ll_wait_cmd_done().  The
59:  * start trigger is not a separate register either: it is the cmd_start bit
60:  * inside each channel's own cfg2 register (cmd_c_cfg2 for the send path,
61:  * cmd_d_cfg2 for the read path), matching qspi_ll_cmd_c_start() and
62:  * qspi_ll_cmd_d_start().
63:  *
64:  * Pinmux: the QSPI1 controller's four signal lines (CLK/CSN/IO0/IO1) are
65:  * shared, multiplexed GPIO pads (GPIO_2/3/4/5 on this SoC), not dedicated
66:  * pins.  Each pad defaults to plain GPIO after reset and must be switched
67:  * to QSPI1 mode via the "second function" pinmux mechanism before the
68:  * controller's TX/RX lines are actually connected to the pad -- without
69:  * this step cmd_start_done never asserts because the panel never receives
70:  * the command.  Source of the function-select index (6) for QSPI1 on
71:  * GPIO_2/3/4/5: bk_avdk_smp release/v3.1.1
72:  * ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/gpio_map.h gpio_map_table (QSPI1_CLK/
73:  * CSN/IO0/IO1 are the 7th entry, index 6, in each pin's per-function
74:  * array).  The pinmux register plumbing itself (BK7258_GPIO_SYS_BASE etc.)
75:  * is shared with bk7258_gpio.c; see bk7258_gpio_set_function().
76:  *
77:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
78:  ****************************************************************************/
79: 
80: #include <nuttx/config.h>
81: #include <nuttx/arch.h>
82: #include <stdbool.h>
83: #include <stdint.h>
84: 
85: #include "arm_internal.h"
86: #include "hardware/bk7258_memorymap.h"
87: #include "hardware/bk7258_sysctrl.h"
88: #include "bk7258_gpio.h"
89: #include "bk7258_qspi.h"
90: 
91: #define QSPI1_CLK_PIN               2u
92: #define QSPI1_CSN_PIN               3u
93: #define QSPI1_IO0_PIN               4u
94: #define QSPI1_IO1_PIN               5u
95: #define QSPI1_PINMUX_FUNCTION       6u
96: 
97: #define QSPI_REG(offset)           (BK7258_QSPI1_BASE + (offset))
98: 
99: #define QSPI_GLB_CTRL              QSPI_REG(0x08u)
100: #define QSPI_GLB_CTRL_SOFT_RESET   (1u << 0)
101: 
102: #define QSPI_CMD_C_L               QSPI_REG(0x40u)
103: #define QSPI_CMD_C_H               QSPI_REG(0x44u)
104: #define QSPI_CMD_C_CFG1            QSPI_REG(0x48u)
105: #define QSPI_CMD_C_CFG2            QSPI_REG(0x4cu)
106: 
107: #define QSPI_CMD_D_L               QSPI_REG(0x50u)
108: #define QSPI_CMD_D_H               QSPI_REG(0x54u)
109: #define QSPI_CMD_D_CFG1            QSPI_REG(0x58u)
110: #define QSPI_CMD_D_CFG2            QSPI_REG(0x5cu)
111: 
112: #define QSPI_STATUS                QSPI_REG(0x70u)
113: #define QSPI_STATUS_CMD_START_DONE (1u << 2)
114: 
115: #define QSPI_STATUS_CLR                 QSPI_REG(0x6cu)
116: #define QSPI_STATUS_CLR_CMD_START_DONE  (1u << 2)
117: 
118: #define QSPI_CMD_START_BIT         (1u << 0)
119: 
120: /* Matches qspi_ll_wait_cmd_done()'s 10000-iteration bound
121:  * (ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/hal/qspi_ll.h) instead of looping forever,
122:  * so a pinmux or wiring problem produces a diagnosable timeout rather than
123:  * an unrecoverable hang. */
124: #define QSPI_WAIT_DONE_MAX_ITER    10000
125: 
126: static bool bk7258_qspi0_wait_done(void)
127: {
128:   int i;
129: 
130:   for (i = 0; i < QSPI_WAIT_DONE_MAX_ITER; i++)
131:     {
132:       if ((getreg32(QSPI_STATUS) & QSPI_STATUS_CMD_START_DONE) != 0)
133:         {
134:           break;
135:         }
136: 
137:       up_udelay(1);
138:     }
139: 
140:   /* Clear cmd_start_done (write 1 then 0), matching qspi_ll_wait_cmd_done()
141:    * -- required so a stale "done" flag from this command does not make
142:    * the next command's wait loop return immediately without having
143:    * actually completed. */
144:   modifyreg32(QSPI_STATUS_CLR, 0, QSPI_STATUS_CLR_CMD_START_DONE);
145:   modifyreg32(QSPI_STATUS_CLR, QSPI_STATUS_CLR_CMD_START_DONE, 0);
146: 
147:   return i < QSPI_WAIT_DONE_MAX_ITER;
148: }
149: 
150: void bk7258_qspi0_init(void)
151: {
152:   /* Enable the QSPI1 *module* clock gate first, matching
153:    * qspi_id_init_common()'s documented call order ("1. set clock, 2. set
154:    * gpio as qspi, 3. enable interrupt") in bk_avdk_smp release/v3.1.1
155:    * ap/middleware/driver/qspi/qspi_driver.c.  Without this bit, register
156:    * writes to the QSPI1 block are accepted (no bus fault) but the
157:    * controller's internal command state machine has no clock to run on,
158:    * so cmd_start_done never asserts -- see
159:    * hardware/bk7258_sysctrl.h's BK7258_QSPI1_MODULE_CLK_EN comment for
160:    * the register-map citation and the I2C1 precedent this is modeled
161:    * after. */
162:   modifyreg32(BK7258_SYS_DEVCLK_EN, 0, BK7258_QSPI1_MODULE_CLK_EN);
163: 
164:   /* Switch the 4 shared GPIO pads to QSPI1 mode before touching the
165:    * controller; see file header comment for why this is required and why
166:    * it is QSPI1 (GPIO2-5) rather than QSPI0 (GPIO22-25) on this board. */
167:   bk7258_gpio_set_function(QSPI1_CLK_PIN, QSPI1_PINMUX_FUNCTION);
168:   bk7258_gpio_set_function(QSPI1_CSN_PIN, QSPI1_PINMUX_FUNCTION);
169:   bk7258_gpio_set_function(QSPI1_IO0_PIN, QSPI1_PINMUX_FUNCTION);
170:   bk7258_gpio_set_function(QSPI1_IO1_PIN, QSPI1_PINMUX_FUNCTION);
171: 
172:   putreg32(QSPI_GLB_CTRL_SOFT_RESET, QSPI_GLB_CTRL);
173:   up_udelay(10);
174:   putreg32(0, QSPI_GLB_CTRL);
175: }
176: 
177: bool bk7258_qspi0_send_cmd(uint8_t cmd, const uint8_t *data, uint8_t data_len)
178: {
179:   uint32_t cmd_c_h = (uint32_t)cmd;
180:   uint32_t cmd_c_l = 0;
181:   uint8_t i;
182: 
183:   putreg32(0, QSPI_CMD_C_L);
184:   putreg32(0, QSPI_CMD_C_H);
185:   putreg32(0, QSPI_CMD_C_CFG1);
186:   putreg32(0, QSPI_CMD_C_CFG2);
187: 
188:   if (data_len > 0 && data_len <= 4)
189:     {
190:       for (i = 0; i < data_len; i++)
191:         {
192:           cmd_c_l |= ((uint32_t)data[i]) << (i * 8);
193:         }
194: 
195:       putreg32(cmd_c_l, QSPI_CMD_C_L);
196:     }
197: 
198:   putreg32(cmd_c_h, QSPI_CMD_C_H);
199:   modifyreg32(QSPI_CMD_C_CFG2, 0, QSPI_CMD_START_BIT);
200:   return bk7258_qspi0_wait_done();
201: }
202: 
203: uint32_t bk7258_qspi0_read_id(void)
204: {
205:   putreg32(0, QSPI_CMD_D_L);
206:   putreg32(0, QSPI_CMD_D_H);
207:   putreg32(0, QSPI_CMD_D_CFG1);
208:   putreg32(0, QSPI_CMD_D_CFG2);
209: 
210:   putreg32(0x04u, QSPI_CMD_D_H); /* GC9D01 read-ID opcode, single byte cmd */
211:   modifyreg32(QSPI_CMD_D_CFG2, 0, QSPI_CMD_START_BIT);
212:   (void)bk7258_qspi0_wait_done();
213: 
214:   return getreg32(QSPI_CMD_D_L);
215: }

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_gc9d01.c
3:  *
4:  * GC9D01 160x160 QSPI LCD panel bring-up.  Init command table copied from
5:  * bk_avdk_smp release/v3.1.1
6:  * ap/components/bk_peripheral/src/lcd/spi/lcd_spi_gc9d01.c (gc9d01_init_cmds,
7:  * 50 entries total).  Only the init sequence is ported; DMA-backed
8:  * full-frame refresh is out of scope for this task.
9:  *
10:  * Command table traceability: bk7258_qspi0_send_cmd() only supports up to
11:  * 4 data bytes per command (see bk7258_qspi.h), which hard-blocks porting
12:  * 11 of the 50 upstream entries whose data_len exceeds 4:
13:  *   0x74(7) 0x64(6) 0x65(6) 0x6C(7) 0x6E(32) 0x70(6) 0xF0(6) 0xF2(6)
14:  *   0xF1(6) 0xF3(6), plus the special 0x00/data_len=0xFF delay marker
15:  *   (handled separately below, not a real QSPI command).
16:  * The remaining 9 omitted entries (0x98, 0xB5, 0x60, 0x61, 0x6A, 0x93,
17:  * 0x71, 0x91, 0x34) all fit within the 4-byte limit and were dropped in
18:  * an earlier revision of this file without a stated reason; upstream
19:  * documents them as gamma/porch/timing fine-tuning registers that are not
20:  * required to reach a functional display state, but this has not been
21:  * independently confirmed against the GC9D01 datasheet.  If the panel
22:  * shows visible artifacts once full-frame refresh is implemented, restore
23:  * these 9 entries first as they are the cheapest to re-add (all <= 4
24:  * bytes, no interface change needed).
25:  *
26:  * One functional gap from an earlier revision of this file has been
27:  * fixed here: upstream sends {0x00, {0x78}, 0xFF} between the Sleep Out
28:  * (0x11) and Display On (0x29) commands.  data_len == 0xFF is not a real
29:  * QSPI command; per bk_lcd_qspi_init() in
30:  * ap/middleware/driver/lcd/lcd_qspi_driver.c, it is a driver-level marker
31:  * meaning "delay data[0] milliseconds" (0x78 = 120ms).  This delay is
32:  * restored below as an explicit up_udelay() call between the two
33:  * commands, since bk7258_qspi0_send_cmd() has no equivalent marker
34:  * convention.
35:  *
36:  * Bus/reset-pin correction (2026-07-31): the very first init command
37:  * (0xFE) was timing out on real hardware.  Root cause was two wrong
38:  * hardware assumptions, both corrected together (diagnosed via the board
39:  * schematic, AIDK_AI玩具开发板_原理图.pdf):
40:  *   1. bk7258_qspi.c was driving QSPI0 (GPIO22-25), but this board's
41:  *      LCD is wired to QSPI1 (GPIO2-5) -- see that file's header comment
42:  *      for the full pin-by-pin schematic evidence.
43:  *   2. GC9D01_RESET_PIN below was GPIO_6 (copied from a different board's
44:  *      dual-screen reference config in BTdocs/DualScreenAVIPlayer.md);
45:  *      the schematic shows GPIO_6 floating (unconnected) on this board,
46:  *      the real LCD_RST net is GPIO45.
47:  * Neither symptom was diagnosable from register-level behavior alone
48:  * (cmd_start_done simply never asserts when the controller drives pins
49:  * the panel isn't wired to); both required cross-checking the schematic
50:  * against gpio_map.h's pinmux function tables.
51:  *
52:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
53:  ****************************************************************************/
54: 
55: #include <nuttx/config.h>
56: #include <nuttx/arch.h>
57: #include <stdbool.h>
58: #include <stdint.h>
59: #include <stdio.h>
60: 
61: #include "bk7258_gpio.h"
62: #include "bk7258_qspi.h"
63: 
64: /* GC9D01 reset pin, corrected against the actual board schematic
65:  * (AIDK_AI玩具开发板_原理图.pdf) after this driver's original QSPI0/GPIO6
66:  * assumption (ported from BTdocs/DualScreenAVIPlayer.md's lcd0 config,
67:  * a *different* board's dual-screen reference layout) caused the very
68:  * first init command (0xFE) to time out -- the panel was never wired to
69:  * the pins this driver was toggling.  The schematic (sheet 2/6 main chip
70:  * pin table) shows GPIO_6 net-labelled nothing at all on this board
71:  * (floating, no connection); the actual LCD_RST net is wired to chip pin
72:  * 65 = P45 = GPIO45 (same sheet's pin table row "P45/0CSN/B5/D2/2LRCK"),
73:  * confirmed again on sheet 5/6's CN5 single-screen connector pin 13
74:  * (labelled LCD_RST). See bk7258_qspi.c's file header for the QSPI0->
75:  * QSPI1 correction that was diagnosed alongside this one (both changes
76:  * were needed to get past the same "cmd 0xFE timed out" symptom). */
77: #define GC9D01_RESET_PIN 45u
78: 
79: /* Post-Sleep-Out settle delay before Display On, per upstream
80:  * gc9d01_init_cmds entry {0x00, {0x78}, 0xFF} (0x78 = 120 decimal ms). */
81: #define GC9D01_SLEEP_OUT_DELAY_MS 120u
82: 
83: struct gc9d01_init_cmd
84: {
85:   uint8_t cmd;
86:   uint8_t data[4];
87:   uint8_t data_len;
88: };
89: 
90: /* Entries below are the 30 upstream commands whose data_len <= 4 and that
91:  * precede the Sleep Out (0x11) command; see file header comment above for
92:  * the full list of the 20 omitted upstream entries and why. */
93: static const struct gc9d01_init_cmd g_gc9d01_init_cmds_pre_sleep_out[] =
94: {
95:   { 0xFE, { 0x00 }, 0 },
96:   { 0xEF, { 0x00 }, 0 },
97:   { 0x80, { 0xFF }, 1 },
98:   { 0x81, { 0xFF }, 1 },
99:   { 0x82, { 0xFF }, 1 },
100:   { 0x83, { 0xFF }, 1 },
101:   { 0x84, { 0xFF }, 1 },
102:   { 0x85, { 0xFF }, 1 },
103:   { 0x86, { 0xFF }, 1 },
104:   { 0x87, { 0xFF }, 1 },
105:   { 0x88, { 0xFF }, 1 },
106:   { 0x89, { 0xFF }, 1 },
107:   { 0x8A, { 0xFF }, 1 },
108:   { 0x8B, { 0xFF }, 1 },
109:   { 0x8C, { 0xFF }, 1 },
110:   { 0x8D, { 0xFF }, 1 },
111:   { 0x8E, { 0xFF }, 1 },
112:   { 0x8F, { 0xFF }, 1 },
113:   { 0x3A, { 0x05 }, 1 },
114:   { 0xEC, { 0x01 }, 1 },
115:   { 0xBF, { 0x01 }, 1 },
116:   { 0xF9, { 0x40 }, 1 },
117:   { 0x9B, { 0x3B }, 1 },
118:   { 0x7E, { 0x30 }, 1 },
119:   { 0xC3, { 0x18 }, 1 },
120:   { 0xC4, { 0x18 }, 1 },
121:   { 0xC9, { 0x3C }, 1 },
122:   { 0x36, { 0x00 }, 1 },
123:   { 0x11, { 0x00 }, 0 }, /* Sleep Out */
124: };
125: 
126: #define GC9D01_PRE_SLEEP_OUT_CMD_COUNT \
127:   (sizeof(g_gc9d01_init_cmds_pre_sleep_out) / \
128:    sizeof(g_gc9d01_init_cmds_pre_sleep_out[0]))
129: 
130: /* Display On (0x29), sent GC9D01_SLEEP_OUT_DELAY_MS after Sleep Out. */
131: static const struct gc9d01_init_cmd g_gc9d01_display_on = { 0x29, { 0x00 }, 0 };
132: 
133: /****************************************************************************
134:  * Name: bk7258_gc9d01_hw_reset
135:  *
136:  * Description:
137:  *   Drive the GC9D01 RESET pin through a high-low-high pulse to force a
138:  *   hardware reset.  Timing: the 10ms pre/post pulse widths are a
139:  *   conservative margin (GC9D01 reset pulse width requirements are
140:  *   typically in the microsecond range; 10ms has no specific datasheet
141:  *   citation but costs nothing at bring-up time).  The final 120ms
142:  *   post-reset settle delay before issuing any command matches the
143:  *   reset-to-ready delay used across every other panel driver in the same
144:  *   bk_avdk_smp codebase (ap/components/bk_peripheral/src/lcd/rgb and .../mcu
145:  *   uniformly use rtos_delay_milliseconds(120) after hardware reset, e.g.
146:  *   lcd_st7701s.c:48, lcd_nt35512.c:859, lcd_st7789v.c:167), i.e. 120ms is
147:  *   the de-facto standard settle time for this class of display driver IC
148:  *   and is not GC9D01-specific tuning.
149:  *
150:  ****************************************************************************/
151: 
152: static void bk7258_gc9d01_hw_reset(void)
153: {
154:   bk7258_gpio_output(GC9D01_RESET_PIN, true);
155:   up_udelay(10000);
156:   bk7258_gpio_write(GC9D01_RESET_PIN, false);
157:   up_udelay(10000);
158:   bk7258_gpio_write(GC9D01_RESET_PIN, true);
159:   up_udelay(120000);
160: }
161: 
162: /****************************************************************************
163:  * Name: bk7258_gc9d01_test
164:  *
165:  * Description:
166:  *   Bring-up smoke test for the GC9D01 panel: hardware reset, QSPI0 init,
167:  *   then send the full init command sequence (pre-Sleep-Out commands,
168:  *   Sleep Out, 120ms settle delay, Display On).  There is no Read ID
169:  *   command in the upstream init table (verified: the only "0x04" bytes
170:  *   found in lcd_spi_gc9d01.c are payload data, not an RDID opcode), so
171:  *   this test cannot verify success by reading back a panel ID.  Success
172:  *   criterion is therefore "the full init sequence is sent without the
173:  *   call hanging or crashing", not a register readback match.
174:  *
175:  ****************************************************************************/
176: 
177: int bk7258_gc9d01_test(int argc, char **argv)
178: {
179:   size_t i;
180: 
181:   printf("gc9d01: hardware reset\n");
182:   bk7258_gc9d01_hw_reset();
183: 
184:   printf("gc9d01: qspi0 init\n");
185:   bk7258_qspi0_init();
186: 
187:   printf("gc9d01: sending %u init commands (through sleep out)\n",
188:          (unsigned int)GC9D01_PRE_SLEEP_OUT_CMD_COUNT);
189:   for (i = 0; i < GC9D01_PRE_SLEEP_OUT_CMD_COUNT; i++)
190:     {
191:       if (!bk7258_qspi0_send_cmd(g_gc9d01_init_cmds_pre_sleep_out[i].cmd,
192:                                  g_gc9d01_init_cmds_pre_sleep_out[i].data,
193:                                  g_gc9d01_init_cmds_pre_sleep_out[i].data_len))
194:         {
195:           printf("gc9d01: qspi0 timed out waiting for cmd 0x%02x "
196:                  "(index %u) to complete, aborting init sequence\n",
197:                  g_gc9d01_init_cmds_pre_sleep_out[i].cmd, (unsigned int)i);
198:           return -1;
199:         }
200:     }
201: 
202:   printf("gc9d01: sleep-out settle delay (%u ms)\n",
203:          GC9D01_SLEEP_OUT_DELAY_MS);
204:   up_udelay(GC9D01_SLEEP_OUT_DELAY_MS * 1000u);
205: 
206:   printf("gc9d01: display on\n");
207:   if (!bk7258_qspi0_send_cmd(g_gc9d01_display_on.cmd,
208:                               g_gc9d01_display_on.data,
209:                               g_gc9d01_display_on.data_len))
210:     {
211:       printf("gc9d01: qspi0 timed out waiting for display-on cmd to "
212:              "complete\n");
213:       return -1;
214:     }
215: 
216:   printf("gc9d01: init sequence completed without hang\n");
217:   return 0;
218: }

1: /****************************************************************************

4: 
5: #include <nuttx/config.h>
6: 
7: #include <errno.h>
8: #include <stdbool.h>
9: #include <stdint.h>
10: 
11: #include <nuttx/irq.h>
12: #include <nuttx/spinlock.h>
13: #include <nuttx/timers/pwm.h>
14: 
15: #include "arm_internal.h"
16: #include "bk7258_gpio.h"
17: 
18: #define BK7258_SYS_CLKSEL             0x44010020u
19: #define BK7258_SYS_CLK_ENABLE         0x44010030u
20: #define BK7258_SYS_PWM0_CLKSEL        (1u << 18)
21: #define BK7258_SYS_PWM0_CLK_ENABLE    (1u << 3)
22: 
23: #define BK7258_PWM0_BASE              0x458a0000u
24: #define BK7258_PWM_CG_RESET           (BK7258_PWM0_BASE + 0x08u)
25: #define BK7258_PWM_CR1                (BK7258_PWM0_BASE + 0x10u)
26: #define BK7258_PWM_EDTR               (BK7258_PWM0_BASE + 0x24u)
27: #define BK7258_PWM_CCMR               (BK7258_PWM0_BASE + 0x28u)
28: #define BK7258_PWM_PRESCALER          (BK7258_PWM0_BASE + 0x38u)
29: #define BK7258_PWM_TIM2_ARR           (BK7258_PWM0_BASE + 0x40u)
30: #define BK7258_PWM_CCR4               (BK7258_PWM0_BASE + 0x60u)
31: #define BK7258_PWM_CCR5               (BK7258_PWM0_BASE + 0x64u)
32: 
33: #define BK7258_PWM_CR1_CEN2           (1u << 1)
34: #define BK7258_PWM_CR1_ARPE2          (1u << 4)
35: #define BK7258_PWM_CR1_OC2PE          (1u << 7)
36: #define BK7258_PWM_EDTR_UG2           (1u << 10)
37: #define BK7258_PWM_CCMR_CH4E          (1u << 15)
38: #define BK7258_PWM_CCMR_TIM2CCM       (1u << 19)
39: #define BK7258_PWM_CCMR_OC2M_MASK     (7u << 24)
40: #define BK7258_PWM_CCMR_OC2M_TOGGLE   (1u << 24)
41: #define BK7258_PWM_CCMR_OC2M_HIGH     (2u << 24)
42: #define BK7258_PWM_CCMR_OC2M_LOW      (4u << 24)
43: #define BK7258_PWM_PSC2_MASK          (0xffu << 8)
44: #define BK7258_PWM_CLOCK_HZ           26000000u
45: 
46: #define BK7258_MOTOR_PWM_GPIO         9u
47: #define BK7258_MOTOR_LDO_GPIO         52u
48: #define BK7258_GPIO_FUNC_PWM3         1u
49: 
50: struct bk7258_pwm_lowerhalf_s
51: {
52:   const struct pwm_ops_s *ops;
53:   bool setup;
54: };
55: 
56: void bk7258_gpio_output(unsigned int pin, bool value);
57: void bk7258_gpio_write(unsigned int pin, bool value);
58: void bk7258_gpio_set_function(unsigned int pin, unsigned int function);
59: 
60: static int bk7258_pwm_setup(struct pwm_lowerhalf_s *dev);
61: static int bk7258_pwm_shutdown(struct pwm_lowerhalf_s *dev);
62: static int bk7258_pwm_start(struct pwm_lowerhalf_s *dev,
63:                             const struct pwm_info_s *info);
64: static int bk7258_pwm_stop(struct pwm_lowerhalf_s *dev);
65: static int bk7258_pwm_ioctl(struct pwm_lowerhalf_s *dev, int cmd,
66:                             unsigned long arg);
67: 
68: static const struct pwm_ops_s g_pwm_ops =
69: {
70:   .setup = bk7258_pwm_setup,
71:   .shutdown = bk7258_pwm_shutdown,
72:   .start = bk7258_pwm_start,
73:   .stop = bk7258_pwm_stop,
74:   .ioctl = bk7258_pwm_ioctl,
75: };
76: 
77: static struct bk7258_pwm_lowerhalf_s g_motor_pwm =
78: {
79:   .ops = &g_pwm_ops,
80: };
81: 
82: static int bk7258_pwm_setup(struct pwm_lowerhalf_s *dev)
83: {
84:   struct bk7258_pwm_lowerhalf_s *priv =
85:     (struct bk7258_pwm_lowerhalf_s *)dev;
86:   irqstate_t flags;
87: 
88:   flags = enter_critical_section();
89:   modifyreg32(BK7258_SYS_CLKSEL, 0, BK7258_SYS_PWM0_CLKSEL);
90:   modifyreg32(BK7258_SYS_CLK_ENABLE, 0, BK7258_SYS_PWM0_CLK_ENABLE);
91:   putreg32(1, BK7258_PWM_CG_RESET);
92:   bk7258_gpio_set_function(BK7258_MOTOR_PWM_GPIO, BK7258_GPIO_FUNC_PWM3);
93:   bk7258_gpio_output(BK7258_MOTOR_LDO_GPIO, false);
94:   priv->setup = true;
95:   leave_critical_section(flags);
96: 
97:   return OK;
98: }
99: 
100: static int bk7258_pwm_shutdown(struct pwm_lowerhalf_s *dev)
101: {
102:   struct bk7258_pwm_lowerhalf_s *priv =
103:     (struct bk7258_pwm_lowerhalf_s *)dev;
104: 
105:   bk7258_pwm_stop(dev);
106:   modifyreg32(BK7258_SYS_CLK_ENABLE, BK7258_SYS_PWM0_CLK_ENABLE, 0);
107:   priv->setup = false;
108:   return OK;
109: }
110: 
111: static int bk7258_pwm_start(struct pwm_lowerhalf_s *dev,
112:                             const struct pwm_info_s *info)
113: {
114:   struct bk7258_pwm_lowerhalf_s *priv =
115:     (struct bk7258_pwm_lowerhalf_s *)dev;
116:   uint64_t period;
117:   uint64_t duty;
118:   irqstate_t flags;
119: 
120:   if (!priv->setup || info == NULL || info->frequency == 0)
121:     {
122:       return -EINVAL;
123:     }
124: 
125:   period = BK7258_PWM_CLOCK_HZ / info->frequency;
126:   if (period < 2 || period > UINT32_MAX)
127:     {
128:       return -ERANGE;
129:     }
130: 
131:   duty = (period * info->duty) >> 16;
132:   if (duty > period)
133:     {
134:       duty = period;
135:     }
136: 
137:   flags = enter_critical_section();
138:   modifyreg32(BK7258_PWM_CR1, BK7258_PWM_CR1_CEN2, 0);
139:   modifyreg32(BK7258_PWM_CR1, 0,
140:               BK7258_PWM_CR1_ARPE2 | BK7258_PWM_CR1_OC2PE);
141:   modifyreg32(BK7258_PWM_PRESCALER, BK7258_PWM_PSC2_MASK, 0);
142:   putreg32((uint32_t)period - 1u, BK7258_PWM_TIM2_ARR);
143:   putreg32((uint32_t)(period - duty), BK7258_PWM_CCR4);
144:   putreg32((uint32_t)period, BK7258_PWM_CCR5);
145:   modifyreg32(BK7258_PWM_CCMR,
146:               BK7258_PWM_CCMR_TIM2CCM | BK7258_PWM_CCMR_OC2M_MASK,
147:               BK7258_PWM_CCMR_CH4E |
148:               (duty == 0 ? BK7258_PWM_CCMR_OC2M_LOW :
149:                duty == period ? BK7258_PWM_CCMR_OC2M_HIGH :
150:                BK7258_PWM_CCMR_OC2M_TOGGLE));
151:   modifyreg32(BK7258_PWM_EDTR, 0, BK7258_PWM_EDTR_UG2);
152:   modifyreg32(BK7258_PWM_CR1, 0, BK7258_PWM_CR1_CEN2);
153:   bk7258_gpio_write(BK7258_MOTOR_LDO_GPIO, duty != 0);
154:   leave_critical_section(flags);
155: 
156:   return OK;
157: }
158: 
159: static int bk7258_pwm_stop(struct pwm_lowerhalf_s *dev)
160: {
161:   irqstate_t flags;
162: 
163:   (void)dev;
164:   flags = enter_critical_section();
165:   modifyreg32(BK7258_PWM_CCMR, BK7258_PWM_CCMR_CH4E, 0);
166:   modifyreg32(BK7258_PWM_CR1, BK7258_PWM_CR1_CEN2, 0);
167:   bk7258_gpio_write(BK7258_MOTOR_LDO_GPIO, false);
168:   leave_critical_section(flags);
169: 
170:   return OK;
171: }
172: 
173: static int bk7258_pwm_ioctl(struct pwm_lowerhalf_s *dev, int cmd,
174:                             unsigned long arg)
175: {
176:   (void)dev;
177:   (void)cmd;
178:   (void)arg;
179:   return -ENOTTY;
180: }
181: 
182: struct pwm_lowerhalf_s *bk7258_pwminitialize(void)
183: {
184:   return (struct pwm_lowerhalf_s *)&g_motor_pwm;
185: }

25: #define BK7258_KEY_POLL_US       5000
26: #define BK7258_KEY_DEBOUNCE_COUNT 6
27: #define BK7258_MOTOR_FREQUENCY   1000
28: #define BK7258_MOTOR_DUTY        ((ub16_t)((7u * 65536u) / 10u))
29: #define BK7258_PM_CLK_CTRL_CMD   2
30: #define BK7258_PM_CLK_ID_PWM_1   3
31: #define BK7258_PM_CLK_POWER_UP   1
32: 
33: struct pwm_lowerhalf_s *bk7258_pwminitialize(void);
34: int bk7258_mailbox_send_pwc(uint8_t command, uint32_t p1, uint32_t p2,
35:                             uint32_t p3);
36: int bk7258_mailbox_wait_pwc(unsigned int timeout_ms);
37: 
38: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_POWER_KEY_MOTOR
39: static sem_t g_motor_ready_sem;
40: static volatile int g_motor_worker_result;
41: 
42: static int bk7258_motor_button_worker(int argc, char **argv)
43: {
44:   struct pwm_info_s info =
45:   {
46:     .frequency = BK7258_MOTOR_FREQUENCY,
47:     .duty = BK7258_MOTOR_DUTY,
48:   };
49:   bool candidate = false;
50:   bool pressed = false;
51:   unsigned int samples = 0;
52:   int ret;
53:   int fd = -1;
54:   clock_t request_start;
55: 
56:   (void)argc;
57:   (void)argv;
58:   request_start = clock_systime_ticks();
59:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_send_pwc(BK7258_PM_CLK_CTRL_CMD,
60:                                 BK7258_PM_CLK_ID_PWM_1,
61:                                 BK7258_PM_CLK_POWER_UP, 0);
62:   if (ret < 0)
63:     {
64:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "power-key motor: PWM clock request failed: %d\n", ret);
65:       goto ready;
66:     }
67: 
68:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_wait_pwc(200);
69:   syslog(LOG_INFO, "power-key motor: PWM clock transport wait=%d elapsed=%lu ms\n",
70:          ret, (unsigned long)TICK2MSEC(clock_systime_ticks() - request_start));
71:   if (ret < 0)
72:     {
73:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "power-key motor: PWM clock ACK failed: %d\n", ret);
74:       goto ready;
75:     }
76: 
77:   nxsig_usleep(20000);
78:   fd = open("/dev/pwm0", O_RDWR);
79:   if (fd < 0)
80:     {
81:       ret = -errno;
82:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "power-key motor: open pwm0 failed: %d\n", ret);
83:       goto ready;
84:     }
85: 
86:   if (ioctl(fd, PWMIOC_SETCHARACTERISTICS,
87:             (unsigned long)(uintptr_t)&info) < 0)
88:     {
89:       ret = -errno;
90:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "power-key motor: set PWM characteristics failed: %d\n",
91:              ret);
92:       close(fd);
93:       goto ready;
94:     }
95: 
96:   ret = OK;
97: 
98: ready:
99:   g_motor_worker_result = ret;
100:   nxsem_post(&g_motor_ready_sem);
101:   if (ret < 0)
102:     {
103:       return ret;
104:     }
105: 
106:   printf("power-key motor worker ready, PWM parameters applied\n");
107: 
108:   for (;;)
109:     {
110:       bool sample = (board_buttons() & BUTTON_POWER_BIT) != 0;
111: 
112:       if (sample != candidate)
113:         {
114:           candidate = sample;
115:           samples = 1;
116:         }
117:       else if (samples < BK7258_KEY_DEBOUNCE_COUNT)
118:         {
119:           samples++;
120:         }
121: 
122:       if (samples == BK7258_KEY_DEBOUNCE_COUNT && pressed != candidate)
123:         {
124:           int cmd = candidate ? PWMIOC_START : PWMIOC_STOP;
125:           clock_t edge_start = clock_systime_ticks();
126: 
127:           if (ioctl(fd, cmd, 0) < 0)

159:    * disabled, so this callback updates UART state directly.
160:    */
161:   command = ack == NULL ? g_uart.transaction_command :
162:             bk7258_mb_header_cmd(ack);
163:   failed = result < 0 || !valid_ack(ack) ||
164:            (ack != NULL && (ack->payload_address & 2u) != 0);
165: 
166:   if (ack != NULL && valid_ack(ack))
167:     {
168:       g_uart.peer_rts = (ack->payload_address & 1u) != 0;
169:       g_uart.peer_rts_known = true;
170:     }
171: 
172:   if (result == -ETIMEDOUT || result == -ECONNRESET)
173:     {
174:       g_uart.peer_rts_known = false;
175:       g_uart.state_pending = true;
176:     }
177: 
178:   if (command == BK7258_MB_UART_DATA && g_uart.tx_inflight != 0)
179:     {
180:       if (!failed)
181:         {
182:           g_uart.tx_read = (g_uart.tx_read + g_uart.tx_inflight) %
183:                            MB_UART_TX_SIZE;
184:           g_uart.tx_retry_count = 0;
185:         }
186:       else if (result == -ETIMEDOUT || result == -ECONNRESET)
187:         {
188:           /* A failed/unknown ACK cannot tell whether CP consumed the bytes.
189:            * Drop this local chunk rather than replaying terminal characters.
190:            */
191: 
192:           g_uart.tx_read = (g_uart.tx_read + g_uart.tx_inflight) %
193:                            MB_UART_TX_SIZE;
194:           g_uart.stats.tx_unknown++;
195:           g_uart.tx_retry_count = 0;
196:           g_uart.stats.resets++;
197:         }
198:       else
199:         {
200:           g_uart.stats.remote_fail++;
201:           g_uart.state_pending = true;
202:           if (g_uart.tx_retry_count == 0)
203:             {
204:               /* Keep tx_read unchanged.  The same chunk may be copied again
205:                * once STATE recovery succeeds, but only once.
206:                */
207: 
208:               g_uart.tx_retry_count = 1;
209:               g_uart.stats.tx_retry++;
210:             }
211:           else
212:             {
213:               g_uart.tx_read = (g_uart.tx_read + g_uart.tx_inflight) %
214:                                MB_UART_TX_SIZE;
215:               g_uart.tx_retry_count = 0;
216:               g_uart.stats.tx_retry_drop++;
217:             }
218:         }
219: 
220:       g_uart.tx_inflight = 0;
221:     }
222:   else if (command == BK7258_MB_UART_STATE && failed)
223:     {
224:       g_uart.stats.remote_fail++;
225:       /* The transport invokes this completion before it changes READY to
226:        * ABORTING.  Always retain a STATE request so RESET recovery has a
227:        * probe to send after it reaches PROBING.
228:        */
229: 
230:       g_uart.state_pending = true;
231:     }
232: 
233:   g_uart.transaction_busy = false;
234:   nxsem_post(&g_uart.worker_sem);
235: }

237: static int mb_uart_receive(const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message,
238:                            uint8_t *ack_flags, void *arg)
239: {
240:   uint8_t command = bk7258_mb_header_cmd(message);
241:   uint16_t length = message->payload_length;
242:   uint16_t first;
243:   bool failed = false;
244:   bool malformed = false;
245: 
246:   (void)arg;
247:   if (ack_flags == NULL)
248:     {
249:       return -EINVAL;
250:     }
251: 
252:   if (command != BK7258_MB_UART_DATA && command != BK7258_MB_UART_STATE)
253:     {
254:       g_uart.stats.bad_flags++;
255:       failed = true;
256:       malformed = true;
257:     }
258:   else if ((message->flags & ~1u) != 0)
259:     {
260:       g_uart.stats.bad_flags++;
261:       failed = true;
262:       malformed = true;
263:     }
264:   else if (message->crc8 != 0)
265:     {
266:       g_uart.stats.bad_crc++;
267:       g_uart.sticky_status |= MB_UART_STATUS_PARITY;
268:       failed = true;
269:       malformed = true;
270:     }
271:   else if (message->reserved != 0)
272:     {
273:       g_uart.stats.bad_reserved++;
274:       failed = true;
275:       malformed = true;
276:     }
277: 
278:   if (!failed && command == BK7258_MB_UART_DATA)
279:     {
280:       if (message->payload_address != BK7258_MB_UART_RX_ADDRESS)
281:         {
282:           g_uart.stats.bad_pointer++;
283:           failed = true;
284:           malformed = true;
285:         }
286:       else if (length == 0 || length > BK7258_MB_UART_CHUNK_SIZE)
287:         {
288:           g_uart.stats.bad_length++;
289:           failed = true;
290:           malformed = true;
291:         }
292:       else if (!bk7258_mailbox_link_ready())
293:         {
294:           failed = true;
295:         }
296:       else if (rx_free() < length)
297:         {
298:           g_uart.stats.rx_overflow++;
299:           g_uart.sticky_status |= MB_UART_STATUS_OVF;
300:           failed = true;
301:         }
302:       else
303:         {
304:           const uint8_t *source =
305:             (const uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)BK7258_MB_UART_RX_ADDRESS;
306: 
307:           __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
308:           first = MB_UART_RX_SIZE - g_uart.rx_write;
309:           if (first > length)
310:             {
311:               first = length;
312:             }
313: 
314:           memcpy(&g_uart.rx_ring[g_uart.rx_write], source, first);
315:           if (first != length)
316:             {
317:               memcpy(g_uart.rx_ring, source + first, length - first);
318:             }
319: 
320:           g_uart.rx_write = (g_uart.rx_write + length) % MB_UART_RX_SIZE;
321:           g_uart.stats.data_rx++;
322:           g_uart.stats.rx_bytes += length;
323:         }
324:     }
325:   else if (!failed)
326:     {
327:       if (message->payload_address != 0 || message->payload_length != 0)
328:         {
329:           g_uart.stats.bad_length++;
330:           failed = true;
331:           malformed = true;
332:         }
333:       else
334:         {
335:           g_uart.stats.state_rx++;
336:         }
337:     }
338: 
339:   if (!malformed)
340:     {
341:       bool old_peer_rts = g_uart.peer_rts;
342: 
343:       g_uart.peer_rts = (message->flags & 1u) != 0;
344:       g_uart.peer_rts_known = true;
345:       if (old_peer_rts && !g_uart.peer_rts)
346:         {
347:           nxsem_post(&g_uart.worker_sem);
348:         }
349:     }
350: 
351:   update_local_rts();
352:   *ack_flags = (g_uart.local_rts ? 1u : 0u) | (failed ? 2u : 0u);
353:   nxsem_post(&g_uart.worker_sem);
354:   return malformed ? -EPROTO : OK;
355: }

357: static int send_state_locked(void)
358: {
359:   struct bk7258_mb_wire_message message;
360:   int ret;
361: 
362:   memset(&message, 0, sizeof(message));

364:                                          BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX);
365:   message.flags = g_uart.local_rts ? 1u : 0u;
366:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_send_wire(BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX, &message,
367:                                   mb_uart_tx_complete, NULL);
368:   if (ret == OK)
369:     {

371:       g_uart.transaction_command = BK7258_MB_UART_STATE;
372:       g_uart.state_pending = false;

379: static int send_data_locked(void)
380: {
381:   struct bk7258_mb_wire_message message;
382:   uint8_t *destination =
383:     (uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)BK7258_MB_UART_TX_ADDRESS;
384:   uint16_t length = tx_count();
385:   uint16_t first;
386:   int ret;
387: 
388:   if (length > BK7258_MB_UART_CHUNK_SIZE)
389:     {
390:       length = BK7258_MB_UART_CHUNK_SIZE;
391:     }
392: 
393:   if (length == 0 || g_uart.peer_rts)
394:     {
395:       return -EAGAIN;
396:     }
397: 
398:   first = MB_UART_TX_SIZE - g_uart.tx_read;
399:   if (first > length)
400:     {
401:       first = length;
402:     }
403: 
404:   memcpy(destination, &g_uart.tx_ring[g_uart.tx_read], first);
405:   if (first != length)
406:     {
407:       memcpy(destination + first, g_uart.tx_ring, length - first);
408:     }
409: 
410:   memset(&message, 0, sizeof(message));
411:   message.header = bk7258_mb_make_header(BK7258_MB_UART_DATA, 0, 0, 0,
412:                                          BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX);
413:   message.payload_address = BK7258_MB_UART_TX_ADDRESS;
414:   message.payload_length = length;
415:   message.flags = g_uart.local_rts ? 1u : 0u;
416:   __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
417:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_send_wire(BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX, &message,
418:                                   mb_uart_tx_complete, NULL);
419:   if (ret == OK)
420:     {
421:       g_uart.transaction_busy = true;
422:       g_uart.transaction_command = BK7258_MB_UART_DATA;
423:       g_uart.tx_inflight = length;
424:       g_uart.stats.data_tx++;
425:     }
426: 
427:   return ret;

430: static int mb_uart_worker(int argc, char **argv)
431: {
432:   (void)argc;
433:   (void)argv;
434: 
435:   for (;;)
436:     {
437:       bk7258_mb_uart_callback_t callback;
438:       void *callback_arg;
439:       irqstate_t flags;
440:       enum bk7258_mb_link_state link;
441: 
442:       (void)nxsem_tickwait_uninterruptible(&g_uart.worker_sem,
443:                                            MB_UART_WORK_INTERVAL);
444:       nxsem_reset(&g_uart.worker_sem, 0);
445:       link = bk7258_mailbox_link_state();
446:       flags = up_irq_save();
447: 
448:       if (!g_uart.transaction_busy)
449:         {
450:           if (link == BK7258_MB_LINK_PROBING && g_uart.state_pending)
451:             {
452:               (void)send_state_locked();
453:             }
454:           else if (link == BK7258_MB_LINK_READY)
455:             {
456:               if (g_uart.state_pending)
457:                 {
458:                   (void)send_state_locked();
459:                 }
460:               else
461:                 {
462:                   (void)send_data_locked();
463:                 }
464:             }
465:         }
466: 
467:       callback = g_uart.callback;
468:       callback_arg = g_uart.callback_arg;
469:       up_irq_restore(flags);
470: 
471:       if (callback != NULL)
472:         {
473:           callback(callback_arg);
474:         }
475:     }
476: 
477:   return OK;
478: }

223: static int send_slot(struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message,
224:                      uint32_t *order)
225: {
226:   uint32_t wire[2];
227:   int ret;
228: 
229:   *order = ++g_send_order;
230:   wire[0] = (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)message;
231:   wire[1] = sizeof(*message);
232:   __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
233:   ret = bk7258_mbox_send(0, wire);
234:   if (ret == OK)
235:     {
236:       g_stats.tx++;
237:     }
238:   else if (ret == -EAGAIN)
239:     {
240:       g_stats.fifo_full++;
241:     }
242: 
243:   if (ret < 0)
244:     {
245:       g_stats.last_tx_error = (uint32_t)(-ret);
246:     }
247: 
248:   return ret;
249: }

286: static void complete_transaction(struct active_transaction *active,
287:                                  const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *ack,
288:                                  int result)
289: {
290:   struct logical_channel *channel = NULL;
291: 
292:   if (active->channel_index < MB_CHANNEL_COUNT)
293:     {
294:       channel = &g_channels[active->channel_index];
295:       channel->queued = false;
296:       channel->result = result;
297:     }
298: 
299:   active->busy = false;
300:   if (result == OK)
301:     {
302:       release_acks_before(active->order);
303:     }
304: 
305:   if (active->callback != NULL)
306:     {
307:       active->callback(ack, result, active->arg);
308:     }
309: }

322:           channel->result = result;

342: static void select_recovery_epoch(void)
343: {
344:   unsigned int i;
345:   struct recovery_epoch *epoch = NULL;
346: 
347:   for (i = 0; i < MB_RECOVERY_SLOT_COUNT; i++)
348:     {
349:       if (!g_recovery[i].probe.quarantine &&
350:           !g_recovery[i].reset_sent && !g_recovery[i].probe.busy)
351:         {
352:           epoch = &g_recovery[i];
353:           g_recovery_index = i;
354:           break;
355:         }
356:     }
357: 
358:   if (epoch == NULL)
359:     {
360:       uint32_t newest = 0;
361: 
362:       for (i = 0; i < MB_RECOVERY_SLOT_COUNT; i++)
363:         {
364:           if (g_recovery[i].probe.order >= newest)
365:             {
366:               newest = g_recovery[i].probe.order;
367:               epoch = &g_recovery[i];
368:               g_recovery_index = i;
369:             }
370:         }
371: 
372:       epoch->replay = true;
373:       g_stats.recovery_replay++;
374:     }
375:   else
376:     {
377:       memset(epoch, 0, sizeof(*epoch));
378:       epoch->reset.header = bk7258_mb_make_header(
379:         0, 0, BK7258_MB_CTRL_ACK_BOX | BK7258_MB_CTRL_RESET, 0,
380:         BK7258_MB_CHAN_HW_CTRL_TX);
381:     }
382: 
383:   g_probe_attempts = 0;
384:   g_reset_pending = !epoch->replay;
385:   g_stats.recovery_cycle++;
386:   set_link_state(epoch->replay ? BK7258_MB_LINK_PROBING :
387:                                  BK7258_MB_LINK_ABORTING);
388: }

390: static void begin_abort(int result)
391: {
392:   struct active_transaction *probe = busy_probe();
393: 
394:   if (g_active.busy)
395:     {
396:       g_active.quarantine = true;
397:       complete_transaction(&g_active, NULL, result);
398:     }
399: 
400:   if (probe != NULL)
401:     {
402:       probe->quarantine = true;
403:       complete_transaction(probe, NULL, result);
404:     }
405: 
406:   fail_pending(result);
407:   g_probe_requested = false;
408:   select_recovery_epoch();
409: }

411: static struct ack_slot *alloc_ack_slot(void)
412: {
413:   unsigned int i;
414: 
415:   for (i = 0; i < MB_ACK_SLOT_COUNT; i++)
416:     {
417:       if (g_ack_slots[i].state == ACK_SLOT_FREE)
418:         {
419:           g_ack_slots[i].state = ACK_SLOT_QUEUED;
420:           return &g_ack_slots[i];
421:         }
422:     }
423: 
424:   g_stats.ack_overflow++;
425:   return NULL;

428: static int dispatch_locked(void)
429: {
430:   struct recovery_epoch *epoch = current_recovery();
431:   struct active_transaction *active;
432:   struct logical_channel *channel;
433:   unsigned int i;
434:   int ret;
435: 
436:   /* ACKs always outrank RESET and ordinary commands. */
437: 
438:   for (i = 0; i < MB_ACK_SLOT_COUNT; i++)
439:     {
440:       if (g_ack_slots[i].state != ACK_SLOT_QUEUED)
441:         {
442:           continue;
443:         }
444: 
445:       ret = send_slot(&g_ack_slots[i].message, &g_ack_slots[i].order);
446:       if (ret < 0)
447:         {
448:           return ret;
449:         }
450: 
451:       g_ack_slots[i].state = ACK_SLOT_SENT;
452:     }
453: 
454:   if (g_reset_pending)
455:     {
456:       ret = send_slot(&epoch->reset, &epoch->reset_order);
457:       if (ret < 0)
458:         {
459:           return ret;
460:         }
461: 
462:       g_reset_pending = false;
463:       epoch->reset_sent = true;
464:       set_link_state(BK7258_MB_LINK_PROBING);
465:     }
466: 
467:   if (g_active.busy || busy_probe() != NULL)
468:     {
469:       return OK;
470:     }
471: 
472:   for (i = 0; i < MB_CHANNEL_COUNT; i++)
473:     {
474:       channel = &g_channels[i];
475:       if (!channel->queued)
476:         {
477:           continue;
478:         }
479: 
480:       if (g_link_state == BK7258_MB_LINK_PROBING)
481:         {
482:           if (g_channel_ids[i] == BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX &&
483:               bk7258_mb_header_cmd(&channel->pending) ==
484:               BK7258_MB_UART_STATE)
485:             {
486:               active = &epoch->probe;
487:             }
488:           else
489:             {
490:               continue;
491:             }
492: 
493:           if (active == &epoch->probe && active->quarantine &&
494:               !epoch->replay)
495:             {
496:               return -ENOLINK;
497:             }
498:         }
499:       else if (g_link_state == BK7258_MB_LINK_READY)
500:         {
501:           active = &g_active;
502:           if (active->quarantine)
503:             {
504:               return -ENOLINK;
505:             }
506:         }
507:       else
508:         {
509:           return OK;
510:         }
511: 
512:       if (!epoch->replay || active != &epoch->probe)
513:         {
514:           memset(&active->message, 0, sizeof(active->message));
515:           memcpy(&active->message, &channel->pending,
516:                  sizeof(active->message));
517:           active->message.header = bk7258_mb_make_header(
518:             bk7258_mb_header_cmd(&channel->pending),
519:             bk7258_mb_header_state(&channel->pending), 0, ++g_tx_seq,
520:             g_channel_ids[i]);
521:         }
522: 
523:       active->callback = channel->callback;
524:       active->arg = channel->arg;
525:       active->channel_index = i;
526:       active->started = clock_systime_ticks();
527:       active->busy = true;
528:       ret = send_slot(&active->message, &active->order);
529:       if (ret < 0)
530:         {
531:           active->busy = false;
532:           return ret;
533:         }
534: 
535:       if (active == &epoch->probe)
536:         {
537:           if (epoch->first_probe_order == 0)
538:             {
539:               epoch->first_probe_order = active->order;
540:             }
541: 
542:           g_probe_attempts++;
543:           g_stats.probes++;
544:         }
545: 
546:       return OK;
547:     }
548: 
549:   return OK;
550: }

552: static uint32_t ack_header_reason(
553:   const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message,
554:   const struct active_transaction *active)
555: {
556:   uint8_t control = bk7258_mb_header_ctrl(message);
557:   uint32_t reason = 0;
558: 
559:   if (!active->busy)
560:     {
561:       return 1u;
562:     }
563: 
564:   if (control != BK7258_MB_CTRL_ACK_BOX)
565:     {
566:       reason |= 2u;
567:     }
568:   if (bk7258_mb_header_channel(message) !=
569:       bk7258_mb_header_channel(&active->message))
570:     {
571:       reason |= 4u;
572:     }
573:   if (bk7258_mb_header_seq(message) !=
574:       bk7258_mb_header_seq(&active->message))
575:     {
576:       reason |= 8u;
577:     }
578:   if (bk7258_mb_header_cmd(message) !=
579:       bk7258_mb_header_cmd(&active->message))
580:     {
581:       reason |= 16u;
582:     }
583: 
584:   return reason;
585: }

587: static bool valid_uart_ack(const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message)
588: {
589:   return (message->payload_address & ~3u) == 0 &&
590:          message->payload_length == 0 && message->flags == 0 &&
591:          message->crc8 == 0 && message->reserved == 0;
592: }
593: 
594: static void handle_ack(const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message)
595: {
596:   struct recovery_epoch *epoch = current_recovery();
597:   struct active_transaction *active;
598:   bool replay;
599:   int result;
600:   uint32_t reason;
601: 
602: 
603:   active = busy_probe();
604:   if (active == NULL)
605:     {
606:       active = &g_active;
607:     }
608: 
609:   g_stats.last_ack_header = message->header;
610:   g_stats.last_active_header = active->message.header;
611:   reason = ack_header_reason(message, active);
612:   if (reason != 0)
613:     {
614:       g_stats.bad_ack++;
615:       g_stats.bad_ack_reason |= reason;
616:       return;
617:     }
618: 
619: 
620:   if (bk7258_mb_header_channel(message) == BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX &&
621:       !valid_uart_ack(message))
622:     {
623:       /* Keep active stable.  A malformed ACK is not an ownership proof. */
624: 
625:       g_stats.bad_ack++;
626:       g_stats.bad_ack_reason |= 32u;
627:       return;
628:     }
629: 
630:   if ((bk7258_mb_header_state(message) & ~BK7258_MB_STATE_COM_FAIL) != 0)
631:     {
632:       g_stats.bad_ack++;
633:       g_stats.bad_ack_reason |= 64u;
634:       return;
635:     }
636: 
637:   result = (bk7258_mb_header_state(message) & BK7258_MB_STATE_COM_FAIL) != 0 ?
638:            -EREMOTEIO : OK;
639: 
640:   if (bk7258_mb_header_channel(message) == BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX &&
641:       result == OK && (message->payload_address & 2u) != 0)
642:     {
643:       result = -EREMOTEIO;
644:     }
645: 
646:   replay = active == &epoch->probe && epoch->replay;
647:   release_acks_before(replay ? epoch->first_probe_order : active->order);
648:   if (replay)
649:     {
650:       unsigned int replay_index = g_recovery_index;
651:       unsigned int i;
652: 
653:       /* This ACK may be a late ACK for the original copy.  It proves every
654:        * older epoch was copied, but not that the new replay envelope was
655:        * copied.  Preserve the replay epoch, free only older epochs, and use
656:        * one of them for a fresh-sequence confirmation probe.
657:        */
658: 
659:       complete_transaction(active, message, -EAGAIN);
660:       g_active.quarantine = false;
661:       for (i = 0; i < MB_RECOVERY_SLOT_COUNT; i++)
662:         {
663:           if (i != replay_index)
664:             {
665:               memset(&g_recovery[i], 0, sizeof(g_recovery[i]));
666:             }
667:         }
668: 
669:       select_recovery_epoch();
670:       (void)dispatch_locked();
671:       return;
672:     }
673: 
674:   complete_transaction(active, message, result);
675: 
676:   if (active == &epoch->probe)
677:     {
678:       if (result == OK && (message->flags & 2u) == 0)
679:         {
680:           release_recovery_slots();
681:           g_recovery_index = 0;
682:           g_probe_attempts = 0;
683:           set_link_state(BK7258_MB_LINK_READY);
684:         }
685:       else if (result == -EREMOTEIO &&
686:                g_probe_attempts < MB_PROBE_MAX_ATTEMPTS)
687:         {
688:           /* CP may not have opened MB_UART0 yet.  The matched ACK proves
689:            * that this probe slot is no longer referenced by its FIFO.
690:            */
691:         }
692:       else
693:         {
694:           g_stats.probe_fail++;
695:           epoch->probe.quarantine = result == -ETIMEDOUT;
696:           set_link_state(BK7258_MB_LINK_DOWN);
697:         }
698:     }
699: 
700:   else if (bk7258_mb_header_channel(message) == BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX &&
701:            result < 0)
702:     {
703:       begin_abort(result);
704:     }
705: 
706:   (void)dispatch_locked();
707: }

709: static int handle_command(const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message)
710: {
711:   struct ack_slot *slot;
712:   unsigned int rx_index;
713:   uint8_t channel = bk7258_mb_header_channel(message);
714:   uint8_t control = bk7258_mb_header_ctrl(message);
715:   uint8_t ack_flags = 0;
716:   uint8_t state = 0;
717:   int ret = -ENOSYS;
718: 
719:   g_stats.last_command_header = message->header;
720: 
721:   if ((control & BK7258_MB_CTRL_SYNC_TX) == 0)
722:     {
723:       slot = alloc_ack_slot();
724:       if (slot == NULL)
725:         {
726:           g_stats.deferred_command++;
727:           return -EAGAIN;
728:         }
729:     }
730:   else
731:     {
732:       slot = NULL;
733:     }
734: 
735:   if ((control & ~(BK7258_MB_CTRL_SYNC_TX | BK7258_MB_CTRL_RESET)) != 0 ||
736:       bk7258_mb_header_state(message) != 0 ||
737:       (channel & 0xf0u) != 0x40u)
738:     {
739:       g_stats.bad_header++;
740:       state = BK7258_MB_STATE_COM_FAIL;
741:     }
742:   else if ((rx_index = rx_channel_index(channel)) < MB_RX_CHANNEL_COUNT &&
743:            g_rx_callbacks[rx_index] != NULL)
744:     {
745:       ret = g_rx_callbacks[rx_index](message, &ack_flags,
746:                                       g_rx_args[rx_index]);
747:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)
748:         {
749:           if (slot != NULL)
750:             {
751:               slot->state = ACK_SLOT_FREE;
752:             }
753: 
754:           g_stats.deferred_command++;
755:           return -EAGAIN;
756:         }
757:       else if (ret < 0)
758:         {
759:           state = BK7258_MB_STATE_COM_FAIL;
760:         }
761:     }
762:   else if (channel == BK7258_MB_CHAN_PWC_RX && g_pwc_rx != NULL)
763:     {
764:       ret = g_pwc_rx(message);
765:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)
766:         {
767:           if (slot != NULL)
768:             {
769:               slot->state = ACK_SLOT_FREE;

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * board/beken/chips/bk7258/include/bk7258_i2c1.h
3:  *
4:  * Interrupt-driven hardware I2C1 master driver.
5:  *
6:  * This replaces the earlier software-simulated (bit-banged) I2C driver
7:  * (bk7258_i2c_sim.c/.h) for GC2145 camera register access.  The switch
8:  * was forced by the board schematic (AIDK_AI玩具开发板_原理图.pdf, sheet
9:  * 4/6 "DVP/SENSOR/NAND/MOTOR/KEY"), which shows GC2145's SCL/SDA wired to
10:  * the chip's *hardware* I2C1 peripheral (network labels IIC1_SCL/
11:  * IIC1_SDA, with 4.7K pull-ups to VDDGPIO) -- not to a pair of plain
12:  * GPIOs that firmware could bit-bang arbitrarily.  The previous driver's
13:  * choice of GPIO0/GPIO1 for bit-banging was based on a reference
14:  * project's default config (bk_avdk_smp dvp_example) that does not match
15:  * this board: GPIO0/GPIO1 are actually wired to UART1_TXD/UART1_RXD here
16:  * (schematic sheet 2/6 pin table), which explains why every prior
17:  * hardware bring-up attempt saw the GC2145 never ACK the first I2C byte
18:  * -- the bit-banged signal was toggling the wrong physical pins.
19:  *
20:  * The real IIC1_SCL/IIC1_SDA nets are routed by the chip's pinmux to
21:  * GPIO42/GPIO43 (bk_avdk_smp ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/gpio_map.h
22:  * GPIO_I2C1_MAP_TABLE's second entry, BIT64(42)|BIT64(43); the first
23:  * entry, GPIO0/GPIO1, is I2C1's *other* selectable pin group used by a
24:  * different board, not this one).  This driver hard-codes GPIO42/43 as
25:  * this board's only wiring; it is not a general-purpose pinmux-selectable
26:  * I2C1 driver.
27:  *
28:  * Architecture: this is a from-scratch reimplementation of the interrupt
29:  * + semaphore master state machine in bk_avdk_smp release/v3.1.1
30:  * ap/middleware/driver/i2c/i2c_driver.c (i2c_hardware_memory_write_impl(),
31:  * i2c_master_isr_common(), i2c1_isr_common()), adapted to NuttX's
32:  * irq_attach()/up_enable_irq()/nxsem_wait() primitives in place of
33:  * Beken RTOS's bk_int_isr_register()/rtos_get_semaphore().  Only the
34:  * master-write path is implemented (I2C_MASTER_WRITE state sequence:
35:  * START -> TX_DEV_ADDR -> TX_MEM_ADDR -> TX_DATA -> STOP); master-read,
36:  * slave mode, 10-bit addressing, and low-power-sleep register
37:  * backup/restore are intentionally omitted, since GC2145 bring-up (585 +
38:  * 40 register writes, all 8-bit register address / 8-bit data, no
39:  * readback) is this driver's only consumer.
40:  */
41: 
42: #ifndef __VENDOR_BEKEN_CHIPS_BK7258_INCLUDE_BK7258_I2C1_H
43: #define __VENDOR_BEKEN_CHIPS_BK7258_INCLUDE_BK7258_I2C1_H
44: 
45: #include <stdbool.h>
46: #include <stdint.h>
47: 
48: /* Initializes the I2C1 peripheral: configures GPIO42/GPIO43 pinmux to
49:  * the I2C1_SCL/I2C1_SDA hardware function (with pull-ups, matching the
50:  * board's 4.7K external pull-up resistors being merely a bus-idle-state
51:  * backstop, not a substitute for internal pull enable), sets the bus
52:  * clock divider for 100kHz standard-mode operation, and attaches/enables
53:  * the I2C1 interrupt.  Must be called once before any
54:  * bk7258_i2c1_write_reg() call. */
55: void bk7258_i2c1_init(void);
56: 
57: /* Writes a single 8-bit value to an 8-bit register address on the 7-bit
58:  * I2C device address i2c_addr, via I2C1.  Blocks (via semaphore wait,
59:  * bounded by an internal timeout) until the hardware state machine
60:  * completes the START/address/register-address/data/STOP sequence and
61:  * reports the transaction's ACK/NACK outcome.  Returns true if every
62:  * byte (device address, register address, data) was ACKed by the slave;
63:  * false on any NACK or SCL-timeout condition (mirroring
64:  * bk7258_i2c_sim_write_reg()'s return convention so callers such as
65:  * bk7258_gc2145_write_reg_table() do not need to change). */
66: bool bk7258_i2c1_write_reg(uint8_t i2c_addr, uint8_t reg, uint8_t value);
67: 
68: #endif /* __VENDOR_BEKEN_CHIPS_BK7258_INCLUDE_BK7258_I2C1_H */
